_comment: Where one SEO pass lands. Most of what this operation produces is a report and changes nothing — but the parts that do change something are split across two repos and a snapshot nobody would think to commit.

paths: the pages, sitemap, robots and metadata the audit named
places.close: commit, then the project's own publish command
places.why_enter: Committing is not publishing: a site whose hosting has git deployment switched off serves the old page until the publish command runs. An SEO fix that is committed and not deployed is a fix that does not exist, and the next audit will report the same finding.

places.note: Search Console indexing requests and any analytics change are the owner's, and rate-limited. Give the exact URLs; let them submit.

order: site (fix, commit, publish, then verify the live page — in that order)
_order_why: Verification before the publish reads the old page and passes, which is the most convincing way to be wrong.
